newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds had given up most of their earlier gains by the close as the strong dollar continued to cap the upside.
Guilder bonds had opened firmer and extended their initial gains after a smaller than expected rise in U.S. June consumer prices of 0.1 percent, compared with an expected 0.2 percent.
But dealers said the dollar's persistent strength and expectations that it would rise further were still triggering flows out of European bond markets and into U.S. Treasuries.
Some dealers predicted European central banks would intervene in forex markets in the short term and would hike interest rates later this year to curb the dollar's rise.

Five and 10-year Dutch yield spreads versus Germany both narrowed by one basis point to -6, and dealers said Dutch and German bond yields could be level by the end of the year if current convergence trends continued in Europe as seemed likely.
